title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Reproducible Ceiling/Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) that measured the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic verifier (+ optional single repair) between an LLM generator and apply for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic task generator and validator we selected K=200 tasks by a reproducible SHA‑256 sorting rule and used a single shared generator output per task. Observed primary outcome: baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies; guarded = 200/200; paired difference = 0.00; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00]. The preregistered hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes versus LLM‑only) is not supported in this tested regime (ceiling/null outcome). All execution and scoring artifacts are archived for replay: raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6580c9df4..., task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce925..., and initial master prompt provenance at provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...; repair calls were never invoked (repair_applied=false in every guarded scoring JSON). We release the archived traces to enable failure‑rich follow‑ups and to clarify design choices that produced the ceiling outcome.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation promises operator productivity gains but risks introducing regressions (reachability loss, service interruption). A standard mitigation architecture is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM proposes commands, a deterministic verifier checks safety and workflow constraints, and a repair stage attempts to correct violations prior to apply. Despite prototypes and position papers advocating verification‑guided pipelines, there are few preregistered causal estimates of a verifier’s marginal effect under a fully archived execution contract. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (cand-002-gvr-loop) that isolates the verifier+repair marginal effect by using a single shared generator output per task and deterministic task/validator tooling. The experiment’s primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired within task).
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents generate–validate–repair and translation→solver designs for NetOps (e.g., Cornetto and other generate–validate–repair position work) and argues for verifier‑centric architectures or for confining LLMs to translation tasks that a solver verifies. Benchmarks and surveys have highlighted that LLMs frequently introduce regressions unless supported by external checking. Our contribution differs: a preregistered, fully artifacted paired run that reports a reproducible ceiling/null outcome for the particular model/validator/task sampling regime and provides deterministic artifacts for auditors.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. The study was preregistered before observing outcomes (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop; preregistration SHA‑256 = a6d73a5c...). Selection and sampling: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced candidate intents; inclusion required validator coverage; selection was deterministic by sorting SHA‑256(intent_string) and choosing the first K=200 unique tasks (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7...). Model and tooling: requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce9255...), adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5.

Shared‑initial paired protocol. For each task we made a single generator call (shared_initial_generation) that produced candidate_c; the same candidate_c was evaluated in both arms. Baseline: candidate_c accepted and scored after apply. Guarded: candidate_c validated before apply; if validation failed the preregistered pipeline permitted at most one repair call (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1) to produce a repaired candidate which the validator rechecked. This shared_initial design isolates the verifier’s marginal effect on fixed generator outputs but intentionally prevents generator adaptation to validator feedback (this choice was preregistered).

Statistical plan and degenerate outcomes. The preregistered confirmatory test was exact McNemar (two‑sided) on paired binary outcomes plus a paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) to produce a 95% percentile CI for the paired difference. When no discordant pairs are observed (n10=n01=0) the empirical paired distribution is degenerate and the bootstrap reproduces that degenerate distribution; the percentile CI becomes a point mass (here [0.00,0.00]) and the McNemar exact test yields p=1.00. We report these exact artifact‑grounded inferentials (bootstrap parameters and seed are archived; see analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d...).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. Planned episodes: 400 (two arms × 200 tasks). Completed episodes: 400; failed episodes: 0. Model calls used: 200 (single shared generator call per task); repair calls were never invoked (repair_applied=false across all guarded scoring JSONs). Primary archived artifacts: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 = 79c91155..., execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce925..., provenance/master_prompt.txt SHA‑256 = 1872df1e....

Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact ground truth). Complete paired counts: complete_pairs = 200. Baseline validator passes = 200/200; guarded validator passes = 200/200. Paired contingency (guarded × baseline): n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 7bc1bd2a...). Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.00,0.00] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = 52a0858d...). The repair pathway was never exercised; repair_applied=false in every guarded scoring JSON (execution/scoring/*.json).

Representative per‑task diagnostics. Each scoring JSON records validator diagnostics useful for audit: parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, normalized_configuration, final_state snapshot, and difficulty metadata (the per‑task difficulty field appears in execution/scoring/*.json; auditors can deterministically aggregate difficulty counts from those files). Representative scoring JSONs (examples) are archived and hashed: execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 3055f874..., task-000002-guarded.json SHA‑256 = 95bddd4f..., task-000003-guarded.json SHA‑256 = d10b415a....
sections.discussion:
Why the ceiling/null outcome occurred (artifact‑grounded interpretation). Three artifact‑supported, non‑exclusive causes explain the observed ceiling: (1) inclusion rule bias: we required validator coverage for task inclusion (the manifest and scoring JSONs record coverage flags), which makes the confirmatory sample biased toward intents the validator already supports; (2) generator quality and single shared candidate: the requested LLM produced candidates that satisfied validator constraints for the selected tasks (model_calls_used=200 and per‑task normalized_configuration equaled the reference in execution/scoring/*.json), so there were no initial failures to trigger repair; (3) an explicit design choice: the shared_initial_generation design fixes the generator output across arms and therefore prevents regeneration in response to validator feedback — this prevents repair‑triggered regenerate workflows from ever occurring and was preregistered. Repair_applied=false for every guarded episode (archived in execution/scoring/*.json), confirming that the pipeline never needed to exercise the repair step under this regime.

Statistical and practical implications. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline failure rate ≈0.20; the observed baseline = 0.0 invalidates that power assumption post hoc. The exact paired inferential outputs (McNemar p=1.00; bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.00]) correctly describe the observed data under the preregistered estimand: we cannot reject the null of zero paired difference because there were no discordant pairs. Importantly, a ceiling/null outcome under these controlled conditions is scientifically meaningful: it indicates that, for this deterministic sample, model, and validator, the verifier did not change the binary validator outcome because the generator outputs already met the deterministic validator constraints.

Guidance for future failure‑rich evaluations (artifact‑grounded recommendations). To detect verifier/repair marginal utility in confirmatory paired estimates, future experiments should: (A) sample or construct failure‑rich distributions (include historical or adversarial misconfigurations within validator coverage); (B) evaluate multiple generator strengths (including weaker models) so baseline error rates are nonzero; (C) consider interactive estimands (permit regeneration after validator feedback) rather than shared_initial designs when the goal is end‑to‑end closed‑loop improvement. All per‑task difficulty metadata and validator traces are archived to enable deterministic replay and construction of failure‑rich subsets (execution/scoring/*.json).
sections.conclusion: Under the preregistered paired protocol (shared_initial_generation; K=200 tasks selected deterministically; requested_model=gpt-5-mini), we observed baseline = 200/200 validator‑compliant applies and guarded = 200/200; the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis H1 (that G→V→R reduces regression‑causing changes vs LLM‑only) is not supported in this tested regime (paired difference = 0.00; McNemar p = 1.00; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.00]). The repair step was never invoked (repair_applied=false across guarded scoring JSONs). This ceiling/null result is reproducible from the archived artifacts (raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 3dfbe1b6..., task_manifest.jsonl SHA‑256 = f1d447b7..., model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = 1acce925..., master_prompt provenance SHA‑256 = 1872df1e...). It does not imply that verifiers are unnecessary in production; rather, it highlights that a confirmatory test of verifier utility must intentionally sample failure‑rich tasks or change the estimand to an interactive closed‑loop setting. We release the full execution, scoring, provider traces, and verifier diagnostics to support follow‑up studies that target failure modes and broader model families.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize to other LLMs without further experiments.
Deterministic selection that required validator coverage biases the confirmatory sample toward tasks the validator supports; this limits external validity to failure‑rich production distributions.

Construct validity depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity; if the validator lacks coverage for realistic regression modes, the binary outcome conflates true safety with validator reach.

Shared_initial_generation fixes generator outputs across arms and prevented generator adaptation; the design therefore measures verifier marginality on fixed candidates rather than closed‑loop end‑to‑end improvement.
Observed ceiling (baseline success = 100%) rendered the preregistered power calculation inapplicable; reported inferentials are descriptive and artifact‑grounded for the tested regime.
